A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Return Capping research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F are readable and support direct comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figures 4–7 report original reinforcement-learning experiments on Betting Game, Autonomous Vehicle, continuous and discrete Guarded Maze, and Lunar Lander.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the additional Autonomous Vehicle analysis in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, cap approximation, reward adjustment and PPO updates remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same CVaR-PPO objective and procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five environments, including the same Guarded Maze variants and modified Lunar Lander scenario. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 4–5 retain expected-value PPO, CVaR-PG and CVaR-PPO as comparators. Figure 6 retains expected-value PPO, CVaR-PPO and MIX, with CVaR-PG omitted in both versions. Newly cited methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Risk levels, environment modifications, training budgets and batching procedures are unchanged, as are the appendix hyperparameter tables. The added sentence in Section 5.1 only directs readers to existing appendix settings.

E4.justification: The minimum-cap sensitivity comparisons in Figures 4–6 and the outlier-inclusive Autonomous Vehicle analysis in Appendix C and Figure 7 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight Autonomous Vehicle seeds and six continuous Guarded Maze seeds. The outlier handling and Appendix C's 95% confidence-interval reporting are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 4–7 retain identical plotted results, and Section 6 retains the same rankings, convergence failures and training-step comparisons. Relocated figures introduce no additional results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Proposition 4.1 and its proof, minimum-cap validity reasoning, and equations in Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about capped-objective equivalence, cap approximation, sample efficiency, empirical performance and the CVaR-PPO baseline.

C2.justification: Section 2 adds an applicability argument contrasting constrained RL's separate reward and cost functions with this work's risk optimisation over one metric. Experimental interpretations and limitations concerning cap sensitivity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract newly provides a code-repository link and states that all code is available. Existing implementation and environment details remain unchanged; repository availability and contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Kim and Min (2024), Ma et al. (2020), and a constrained-RL paragraph citing Stooke et al. (2020), Yang et al. (2021), and Wu et al. (2024). This modestly expands prior-work coverage and explains the distinction from reward-and-cost constraint formulations.

P1.justification: v2 adds the related-work paragraph, code-access sentence, appendix hyperparameter pointer, acknowledgements and conference publication text. The remaining prose and section organisation are largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Text reflow relocates Figures 3–6 from pages 5–8 to pages 6–9; Figure 6 now appears among references. Figure designs, captions and table structures remain unchanged, and all six appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: The new code-access information and expanded related-work discussion modestly improve reproducibility documentation and contextual clarity. The scientific methods, proofs and evidence remain unchanged. Figure 6's displacement into the references is a small presentation drawback, but the overall documentary gains support a limited improvement.
